rules.title: New Jersey Security Deposit Law - Maximum Security Deposit
rules.requirement: A landlord in New Jersey cannot collect a security deposit of more than one and a half times one month's rent from a tenant.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to most residential rental properties, including mobile homes; excludes owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings unless the tenant requests coverage.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings, unless the tenant sends a written request to the landlord 30 days before the Security Deposit Law provisions apply.
rules.quoted_span:
The maximum-security deposit to be collected by the landlord cannot be more than 
one and one-half times one month’s rent ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 ).

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether the dwelling is owner-occupied (two- or three-family dwelling)
